description: Conception happens this week – it's the official start of your baby's origin story.
Your developing baby just made the journey from fallopian tube to uterus. Welcome!
It's officially time to take a test and see if those two lines are about to change your life.
Now's the time to find a doctor or midwife you vibe with and get that first prenatal visit on the books.
Your baby's heart is officially starting up.
The features – eyes, nose, and mouth – that will make up your cutie's face are starting to look more defined.
Nerves, bones, and muscles are developing inside your baby's tiny limbs right now.
Your placenta is finally ready to produce hormones that help your baby grow.
You might head in for NIPT bloodwork this week – it's a simple way to check in on your baby's health.
All your baby's vital organs are now in place, and many have already started working.
You may hear your baby's heartbeat with a Doppler for the first time at your next checkup.
You can't feel it, but your breasts may have started making colostrum, the nutrient-rich fluid that feeds your baby just after birth.
You're officially in the second trimester!
Your baby is looking more like a little person every day, complete with eyelashes, eyelids, and tiny nails.
Your baby's heart is pumping about 25 quarts of blood a day, which is a serious flex for someone that size.
Your baby's skeleton is hardening from cartilage to bone, so make sure you're getting enough calcium.
You officially need about 340 extra calories a day now to keep up with your baby's growth.
You may start to feel those first little flutters that let you know your baby is on the move.
The mid-pregnancy anatomy scan usually happens around now. You'll get to see your baby up close in this extended ultrasound.
Your baby can hear you now, starting with the steady rhythm of your heartbeat and your voice.
Baby hair is now visible on your little one's head. (They have eyebrows, too!)
Your baby is starting to hear sounds from outside your body, including other people's voices.
You'll likely have a glucose screening test this month to check for gestational diabetes.
This is a great week to start planning your baby shower and getting those invites out.
Your baby is practicing breathing by inhaling and exhaling small amounts of amniotic fluid.
Your baby will likely open their eyes for the first time this week.
Welcome to the third trimester. You're in the home stretch!
It's time to start doing kick counts to keep tabs on your baby's daily movement patterns.
Your partner (or another loved one) can feel your baby kicking from the outside now.
Now's a great time to get your Tdap shot to protect your baby's health.
Have you gotten a pediatrician yet? Here's how to find the best doc for your baby.
It's time to write a birth plan to let your medical team know your preferences.
Your baby can now respond to sound, light, and touch.
Check "install car seat" off your to-do list this week to make sure you're ready for the drive home.
Pack your hospital bag now – don't forget the long charging cable and your favorite snacks.
Your pregnancy has officially reached early term, which means the finish line's in sight.
Your baby is using these final weeks to get their brain and lungs fully prepped for their big debut.
You're officially full term, meaning your baby is ready to thrive after delivery.
Make sure your baby's first checkup is on the calendar for this week.
You and baby may be settling into a sleep, eat, repeat routine this week – and that's a good thing.
Your baby should be back to their birth weight about now! If you've got any of those tiny newborn outfits left, use them while you still can.
You're in the thick of middle-of-the-night feeds right now. They're exhausting, yes, but this phase is helping your little one grow at a record pace.
You've officially survived the first month! Your baby is starting to stay awake a bit longer to take in the world.
Your baby is finding their voice this week and practicing for their first real coos.
It's time for your 6-week postpartum checkup; be honest with your provider about how you're feeling, physically and mentally.
You might get your first real social smile this week, and honestly, it's a total game-changer for the 2 a.m. wake-up calls.
Your baby is due for their 2-month well visit. It's an essential check-in on their growth and development.
This is when your little sidekick starts to realize they have hands – watch for them grabbing at their own fingers, or maybe a fistful of your hair.
If you're heading back to work soon, this is a great week to do a dry run with your childcare provider to ease into the transition.
You've officially survived the fourth trimester. You might notice your baby is more alert and starting to "coo" - their way of joining the group chat.
You've reached the 3-month mark! Your baby's neck muscles are getting so strong, helping them look all around.
Your baby is becoming more coordinated and might even push up during tummy time now.
Your baby is starting to track objects with their eyes, so those colorful toys are finally becoming interesting.
Many babies go through a sleep regression around 4 months; if your champion sleeper is suddenly awake all night, you aren't alone.
It's time for the 4-month checkup. Get ready to talk about starting solids soon - a whole new, messy adventure awaits.
Your baby might be rolling from tummy to back now, so keep a close eye on them during diaper changes.
Drool production might ramp up right now because new teeth are on the way.
Your baby is starting to understand object permanence, meaning they'll look for a toy if you hide it under a blanket.
At 5 months old, your baby may have doubled their birth weight.
Your baby is now old enough to enjoy a good, old-fashioned game of peekaboo.
It's a good week to test out the highchair for the first time (assuming your baby can sit up with a little help).
Your baby is closing in on their half birthday. Now that their depth perception is improving, they can reach for toys much more accurately.
It's time for the 6-month well visit - your baby will get a full physical plus some important vaccines to keep them healthy.
Most babies get their first tooth around now. Once it appears, it's time to start brushing.
Your baby might start sitting up without support now, which gives them a whole new perspective on their toy basket.
Separation anxiety often kicks in around now; it just means your baby knows you're their favorite person.
Now that they're 7 months old, your baby is likely army crawling - it's time to gate off stairs and cover outlets if you haven't already.
Your baby is practicing their pincer grasp these days, using their thumb and forefinger to pick up small pieces of food.
Your baby is starting to understand the word "no," even if they choose to ignore it.
This is about when your baby will get better at self-soothing, which might mean slightly longer stretches of sleep for everyone.
Your baby is now 8 months old. Growth might slow down due to all of their movement and play.
Strap in: Your baby might hit the 8-month sleep regressionright around now.
If you haven't yet, lower the crib mattress to the lowest setting this week for your little gymnast's safety.
Baby's first year is about 75% through. At this age, your baby is becoming a master of imitation - watch what you do, because they're definitely copying your moves.
It's time for the 9-month checkup - the pediatrician will check on those crawling and standing skills.
Your baby might be "cruising" now, using the furniture to shuffle around the room like a pro, so now's a good time to add bumpers to sharp corners.
Clapping and waving "bye-bye" are major social milestones that usually pop up around the 9-month mark.
Right around now is when your baby might stand alone for a few seconds. Get the camera ready!
At 10 months old, your baby is starting to understand simple instructions like "give me the ball."
Your baby is nearing their first birthday! It's time to start thinking about party plans for a 1-year celebration.
This is when your baby might make some early walking attempts. Make sure you have some shoes with flexible soles to help them find their footing.
If you're using an infant car seat, check the weight and height limits this week. Your baby might hit the max soon.
Your baby is 11 months old! They might be able to say two or three clear words now - it's the beginning of some very real conversations.
Your baby is almost ready to transition to a sippy or straw cup or bottle. Order a few options now to have them on hand.
Your baby's starting to get what you're saying - simple directions like "pick up the ball" might actually click now.
It's about time for the 12-month well-baby visit to measure all the growth (physical and otherwise) that happened this year.
Happy first birthday! You've survived the first year of parenthood - take a second to realize how far you've both come.
